Every snapshot directory ships the same delta in three RDF serialisations.

## Formats

| File              | Format        | When to use |
|-------------------|---------------|-------------|
| `delta.ttl`       | Turtle        | Human-readable, compact; default for browsing/editing |
| `delta.nt`        | N-Triples     | Streaming / line-oriented ingestion; no prefix declarations |
| `delta.jsonld`    | JSON-LD       | Web/JS consumers; embeddable in JSON pipelines; links to schema.org context |

## Side-by-side

The same statement (a barangay's English label) in all three formats, as actually shipped in
`2023-10-24/`. Turtle is compact with prefix declarations; N-Triples is fully expanded and
line-oriented; the JSON-LD is shipped in **expanded** form (full URIs, no `@context`).

**Turtle** (`delta.ttl`):

```turtle
@prefix skos: <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#> .

<https://psgc.gov.ph/entity/1381500036> skos:prefLabel "Rizal"@en .
```

**N-Triples** (`delta.nt`) — every term fully spelled out:

```ntriples
<https://psgc.gov.ph/entity/1381500036> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#prefLabel> "Rizal"@en .
```

**JSON-LD** (`delta.jsonld`) — expanded, one node per object:

```json
{
  "@id": "https://psgc.gov.ph/entity/1381500036",
  "http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#prefLabel": [
    { "@language": "en", "@value": "Rizal" }
  ]
}
```

## Consistency across snapshots

The three serialisations are generated from the same in-memory graph. Treat the Turtle file as
canonical when the three disagree.
